chunks: "Yes. In my [your project, e. g. senior design / a club robot / a personal board] I had a board with [e. g. a 0603 LDO and a QFN motor driver] that didn't power up correctly.
Using the multimeter I found [e. g. the 3. 3 volts rail sagging to 1. 1 volts], and the thermal camera or touch test showed [part] heating.

I swapped the [part] with a hot-air station: flux on the pads, board on a preheater to roughly 100 degrees, 350 degree air with low airflow, Kapton tape on the neighbouring parts, and lifted the part when the joints flowed.
Then I cleaned the pads with braid and flux, tinned one pad, placed the new part and reflowed. The first try [honest detail: e. g.
I lifted a pad on the output cap because I pried before the solder was fully molten]. I fixed it with a short piece of 30 gauge wire to the trace.
The lesson was to wait for all joints to be liquid and use more flux. I verified with a microscope and by measuring the rail again, and then went back to find why it failed.
It turned out [root cause, e. g. I'd reversed a cap footprint], so I fixed the footprint in the layout for the next spin.

If I'm being honest, my experience is mostly hand soldering and some hot-air on prototypes, not production-line BGA rework, but I understand how that works: preheat, a profile above liquidus, X-ray afterwards."
